headline: YOUTUBE LOST 13.7 PERCENT OF ITS LIVE HOURS IN ONE QUARTER AND THREE RIVALS GAINED SHARE.  THE WORLD CUP EXPLAINS MOST OF IT, AND THE REPORT NEVER MENTIONS THE WORLD CUP
deck: Streams Charts published its third-quarter numbers this morning and the headline is a record total.  Underneath it, the biggest live platform on earth shed more than two billion hours of watch time in three months while three rivals gained share.  Most of that is one football tournament leaving the comparison.  Exactly one platform's rise survives the explanation.
tldr: YouTube's live hours fell 13.7 percent in one quarter and its share went from 49.5 to 43 percent, but the quarter it is being compared against held 79 of the World Cup's 104 matches, so the fall measures a tournament ending rather than an audience leaving.  Ask any seller quoting third-quarter growth what share of their second-quarter hours was World Cup before you read the percentage.

TikTok LIVE added roughly 1.7 billion hours in three months to a record 33.5 percent of all tracked live viewing, which is the only platform move the World Cup does not explain.  Price a TikTok LIVE version of your next live sponsorship alongside the Twitch and YouTube versions so you have a real comparison.

In one advertiser's campaign, creative that referenced the programme it ran inside returned a cost per sale of 62.08 dollars against 79.05 for creative that did not, needing 30 percent fewer impressions per conversion with everything else held still.  Rewrite the first line of your next creator integration so it names what that specific video is about, and brief one version per subject rather than one master read.

WARC's video row is growing 2.9 percent and is 76 percent television, while social is growing 21.3 percent to 394.6 billion dollars and holds all the creator and social video money with no platform split published.  Quote the social row and the television row when you make the case for owned video, and move social video out of any internal category you benchmark against television.

A crypto casino says it bought a six-month posting ban from a creator with 15 million subscribers, and he says he signed without reading it.  Add a written confirmation that no existing agreement restricts posting during your campaign window, and require it before the deposit goes out.

Aveeno cut strategy brief writing from 30 days to three using AI-built consumer panels, and the chief executive who sells them says large language models return the most common answer.  Use the synthetic panel to kill the weak concepts fast, and book a human panel for the one concept you plan to produce.

There are exactly three ways to structure a creator content deal — work-for-hire, licence and co-production — and a broadly written assignment clause can reach the creator's name and persona.  Name the structure in the first line of your next term sheet, and price a licence rather than a buyout when the format is one the creator already runs.

**THE FEED** · Tuesday 13 October 2026

**YOUTUBE LOST 13.7 PERCENT OF ITS LIVE HOURS IN ONE QUARTER AND THREE RIVALS GAINED SHARE.  THE WORLD CUP EXPLAINS MOST OF IT, AND THE REPORT NEVER MENTIONS THE WORLD CUP**
Streams Charts published its third-quarter numbers this morning and the headline is a record total.  Underneath it, the biggest live platform on earth shed more than two billion hours of watch time in three months while three rivals gained share.  Most of that is one football tournament leaving the comparison.  Exactly one platform's rise survives the explanation.

**1.** YouTube's live hours fell 13.7 percent in one quarter and its share went from 49.5 to 43 percent, but the quarter it is being compared against held 79 of the World Cup's 104 matches, so the fall measures a tournament ending rather than an audience leaving.  Ask any seller quoting third-quarter growth what share of their second-quarter hours was World Cup before you read the percentage.
**2.** TikTok LIVE added roughly 1.7 billion hours in three months to a record 33.5 percent of all tracked live viewing, which is the only platform move the World Cup does not explain.  Price a TikTok LIVE version of your next live sponsorship alongside the Twitch and YouTube versions so you have a real comparison.
**3.** In one advertiser's campaign, creative that referenced the programme it ran inside returned a cost per sale of 62.08 dollars against 79.05 for creative that did not, needing 30 percent fewer impressions per conversion with everything else held still.  Rewrite the first line of your next creator integration so it names what that specific video is about, and brief one version per subject rather than one master read.
**4.** WARC's video row is growing 2.9 percent and is 76 percent television, while social is growing 21.3 percent to 394.6 billion dollars and holds all the creator and social video money with no platform split published.  Quote the social row and the television row when you make the case for owned video, and move social video out of any internal category you benchmark against television.
**5.** A crypto casino says it bought a six-month posting ban from a creator with 15 million subscribers, and he says he signed without reading it.  Add a written confirmation that no existing agreement restricts posting during your campaign window, and require it before the deposit goes out.
**6.** Aveeno cut strategy brief writing from 30 days to three using AI-built consumer panels, and the chief executive who sells them says large language models return the most common answer.  Use the synthetic panel to kill the weak concepts fast, and book a human panel for the one concept you plan to produce.
**7.** There are exactly three ways to structure a creator content deal — work-for-hire, licence and co-production — and a broadly written assignment clause can reach the creator's name and persona.  Name the structure in the first line of your next term sheet, and price a licence rather than a buyout when the format is one the creator already runs.
